note: Five strategies over one ranking, each a different way to control risk. All rebalance monthly — buy on the first trading day, hold to the first of next month — matching how the desk actually trades. #1 drives the Trade Plan; change it from the Compare tab and commit this file.
designNote: These are five approaches, NOT a ladder where each beats the last. Under honest monthly rebalancing (the real rule) the ranking is not monotonic — position sizing, basket width, the sector cap and conviction weighting each help in some periods and cost in others. The Compare tab shows the real numbers; trust the live track over the backtest. Filters that merely repeat the score (MACD, relative strength, above-50-DMA) were tested and dropped.

strategies.name: Core
strategies.blurb: The plainest possible version: rank the universe, buy the top 7 in equal rupee amounts, stop at 2.5x ATR. A control, not a recommendation — it exists so the layers above it have something to prove themselves against.
strategies.adds: Baseline control. Everything else is measured against this.

strategies.name: Equal risk
strategies.tagline: Top 7, equal risk each — your current plan
strategies.blurb: Same seven names, sized by 1 divided by ATR so a stock that swings 5% a day gets a smaller position than one that swings 2%. This is exactly what the Trade Plan has been running: top 7 by composite, inverse-ATR sizing, stop at 2.5x ATR, no filters.
strategies.adds: Position sizing. Equal money means the wildest name quietly decides your month.

strategies.name: Spread
strategies.blurb: Widens the basket from 7 names to 10 — the three that would otherwise sit on the bench get bought too. Same equal-risk sizing.
strategies.adds: Diversification. One bad name does less damage when it is a tenth of the book instead of a seventh.

strategies.name: Balanced
strategies.blurb: Spread, plus a cap of two names from any one sector. The score ranks companies one at a time and has no idea it just handed you four auto-component stocks.
strategies.adds: Concentration control — the risk a per-stock score structurally cannot see.

strategies.name: Consensus
strategies.blurb: Every stock gets a vote from the four strategies above — a vote means that strategy would hold it. On all four shortlists = full position. On three = half position. Fewer than three = skipped. If fewer than ten names qualify it holds fewer and keeps the rest in cash rather than forcing the basket full.
strategies.adds: Conviction weighting, on top of equal-risk sizing and the sector cap.

primaryNote: On the corrected 2-year backtest, Consensus (S5) — the concentrated basket of names all four strategies agree on — led on both return and drawdown, with Equal risk (S2, the plan already being run) close behind. But a backtest is a rehearsal and these numbers are highly sensitive to rebalance timing, so #1 stays on the current plan until the live track earns a change.
